rows.prompt: What is Useful Bot?

tool_calls.name: web_fetch
tool_calls.args: {"url":"https://github.com/wasimjalali/usefulbot"}

rows.reply:
Useful Bot is the app I run in: a team of AI bots that lives on your Mac, one bot per job (writing, research, inbox, files), each with its own chat, instructions and memory, and able to hand work to each other.

The short version:

- **Local first**: chats, bots, memory and generated files stay on your Mac. Nothing is tracked; no analytics or ads. What leaves it is only what a turn sends to your model provider, plus whatever tools you use (web search, connected apps).
- **Any model**: you plug in what you already pay for, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Claude, Gemini, OpenRouter, or a local model on the Mac, and switch per chat. That's how it works with me running on GLM right now.
- **Permission by bot**: each chat runs Read only, Auto or Full access. Anything outside its lane waits for your approval as a card.
- **Your apps**: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack, Notion and hundreds more via connectors (currently blocked until you paste a Composio key in Connectors).
- **Routines**: standing jobs a bot runs on a schedule, like a morning brief.
- **Open source**: it's AGPL-3.0, public at github.com/wasimjalali/usefulbot; a changed build that's distributed or served over a network must keep the source open under the same license. Companies wanting an exception buy a commercial license from Useful Build (hello@usefulbuild.com).

Source: I pulled that from the project's own GitHub README just now.

rows.prompt: Where are my chats and notes stored?
rows.reply:
On this Mac, locally:

- **Chats**: stored by the Useful Bot app itself, under the app's own install folders (`Library/Application Support`), along with bot profiles and their transcripts.
- **My notes**: `~/.useful-bot/` is where the app keeps its state, including the memory notes for bots like me. Same place holds things like `routines.json` and provider connections.
- **Files the bots make** (images, drawings): the Library, `~/Documents/Useful Bot/<bot>/<year-month>/`.

None of it goes to Useful Build; the only thing they receive is feedback you choose to send from Settings. What does leave this Mac is just each turn to your model provider (whatever model is running the chat), plus the tools that get used, such as web search or connected apps.

Note also: those app storage areas are refused to me in every permission mode, so I can't and won't read through your chat store myself.

rows.prompt: What is the difference between Read only, Auto and Full access?
rows.reply:
They're the permission setting per chat, and they decide what I can do without asking you each time:

**Read only**
I can only look. Every change, whether a file write, a shell command that changes anything, an app change (routines, bots, memory) or a connector write, is refused. I can still read files, list folders, run read-only commands (`ls`, `git status`...) and read from connected apps.

**Auto** (the default, and what this chat runs on)
Everyday work with your approval by exception. Inside an attached folder, creating files, building, testing and committing just run. A card comes up only for the riskier things: deleting, git history rewrites, anything that reaches outside the folder or feeds code to an interpreter. In connected apps, reads are free but writes (send, create) ask, and destructive actions (delete, archive, revoke) always ask.

**Full access**
Everything runs without a card: writes anywhere on the Mac, deletes, git rewrites, connector writes, other chats' bots. The one thing that still asks is a wipe aimed at a disk, a top-level folder or a home directory; nothing else isoppable. Credential stores (`.env`, `.ssh`, the keychain, the app's own stores) stay refused in every mode, including this one.

One rule across all three: the setting is yours, never mine to widen. If a task needs a higher mode, you change it in the composer, not me.

rows.prompt: Can you run on a schedule while I'm away?
rows.reply:
Yes, through routines. A routine is a standing instruction a bot runs on a schedule, entered as a turn in that bot's own chat, like a teammate working while you're away.

- **When**: weekly, daily or one-shot schedules, stored as wall-clock time in a timezone, so 09:00 stays 09:00 across clock changes.
- **What**: any recurring job, a morning brief, checking your inbox, a weekly cleanup or a status roll-up.
- **How**: create and edit them in the chat details pane (the info button in the chat header), or ask me and I'll set one up.
- **Testing**: a Test run button runs it once now, outside the schedule, without using the next slot. Pausing stops the schedule but not the test button.
- **Limits**: a run has an hour to finish and is stopped if the session goes quiet for ten minutes. If the Mac sleeps through its window, it catches up with one run, not one per missed window, and a sleeping Mac means downtime generally.

One important caveat: routines run with the same permission the chat has. A routine I'd run at 09:00 can still only do what Auto allows, so writes in connected apps would wait for your approval rather than going through.

Want an example? Name the job and the time and I'll set it up.
